problem_statement: The paper frames the problem as classically simulating the dynamics of noisy, open quantum circuits and other open-system evolutions efficiently. It emphasizes that real-world quantum hardware is affected by environmental noise, so one must simulate master-equation dynamics rather than ideal closed-system circuits.
problem_statement_quotes:
While ideal circuits follow closed-system
models, real-world quantum hardware is inevitably af-
fected by environmental noise, necessitating open quan-
tum system theory [1–4].

Our approach improves the efficiency of classical
simulation of gate-based quantum computing, quantum
annealing, and general open system dynamics.
classical_baseline: The paper compares against direct numerical integration of the master equation, quantum trajectory methods, and tensor-network based algorithms. It treats these as the existing classical approaches for noisy quantum circuit simulation and open-system dynamics.

Several approximate methods address this scaling chal-
lenge. The quantum trajectory (QT) method [8–10] of-

by unraveling system-bath interactions into stochastic
processes, but struggles to converge when Eq. (1) vi-
olates complete positivity (CP) [11].

Tensor-network
based algorithms [12–15] represent quantum states, op-
erations, and noise channels as interconnected tensors
that can be efficiently contracted to compute expecta-
tion values while maintaining favorable scaling, but their
performance degrades significantly with growing entan-
glement, limiting their scalability with increasing circuit
depth [16].
classical_difficulty: The paper says the classical difficulty is mainly scaling and convergence: direct density-matrix evolution has O(D^2) memory cost and is limited to about 10 qubits, QT only reduces memory to O(D) but can fail to converge when complete positivity is violated, and tensor-network methods degrade as entanglement and circuit depth grow. It also notes that non-Markovian dynamics can produce negative jump probabilities, causing QT to fail even at short times.
